characters.name: Alan B'Stard
characters.description: Backhanded Apology: Delivers one inNatural Selectiontowards his rival Ken Price after he’s succeeded in destroying his company and political career before it even started. Even more cruel considering just before this he makes it clear he can’t dig himself out of his situation.And if you’re watching this, Ken… I’mreallysorry. The Bad Guy Wins: He's theVillain Protagonist, and the series ends with him taking over Britain. Bad People Abuse Animals: Amongst his many misdeeds are decapitating his dog for peeing on a poster, running over peacocks, and throwing a cat out of a window. Appropriate behaviour for aCorrupt Politician. Every Man Has His Price: A strong belief of B'Stard's.Policeman: I know why those cars crashed, B'Stard, and I know you know why they crashed.B'Stard: How much do you want? £20,000. Dark and Troubled Past: It is clear fromKeeping Mumthat his mother was heavily abusive to him, to the point he forced her at gunpoint to sign a contract to leave him alone. When she points a knife at his neck, he casually remarks “there’s the mummy I know and love,” implying that this is not the first time this has happened. The incest at the end of the episode further implies this descended to sexual abuse.

characters.name: Piers Fletcher-Dervish
characters.description: The Ditz: Everyone in the show, apart from his fiancée, considers him stupid and oblivious. Everybody Hates Mathematics:But half of £2000 is... (taps on a calculator)0.0057389. Manchild: Keeps a teddy bear and is often quite ignorant of situations. It takes a long time for him to become corrupt under Alan's influence — and even then, he is barely much of a threat. Nice Guy: He's always polite to everyone and tries his best to be kind, even to people like Alan. Oh, Crap!: The years between the events of Seasons 3 and 4 clearly took a toll on Piers. When he hears Alan’s voice for the first time in three years, he immediately starts panicking.

characters.name: Sir Stephen Baxter
characters.description: Literal-Minded: As shown in the first episode.Baxter: ...armed only with his sturdy truncheon, his whistle, and his considerable courage.B'Stard: Old hat.Baxter: Oh, you really think so? Alright. (writing) Armed only with his whistle, his considerable courage, and his old hat. Origins Episode: Downplayed. In an episode in which Alan tries to take down the Welsh Secretary Goronwy Hopkins, it's revealed that Sir Stephen used to be his friend. One day, Hopkins wanted to break off an affair he had, but sent Baxter in his place. A photographer caught the two, the resulting scandal ending any hopes in Baxter gaining any career prospects, and he was on the backbenches ever since, leaving him embittered, especially towards Hopkins, who just kept climbing the political ladder. Put on a Bus: In "Live from Westminister", he decides to accept a peerage in the House of Lords after seeing Piers inflating a blow-up doll of Alan suggestively, and is subsequently never seen again. Rambling Old Man Monologue: Tends to start talking even when he doesn't need to.Dear sorry, old boy! I won't say another word. (six-second pause) Extraordinary, really.

characters.name: Sir Greville Mc Donald
characters.description: Attempted Homewrecker: Has been in an on-off affair with Sarah B'Stard, including during Alan's attempted execution. When Alan himself finds out, he blackmails Greville into stopping it. Older and Wiser: As generally presented by his appearances and much more moderate view of the Conservatives as compared to B'Stard's radical views.

characters.name: The Chief Whip
characters.description: Married to the Job: Appears this way considering he isn’t married. It’s most likely being closeted meant he put his attention into his career instead. Straight Gay: In Season 2 he admits to Alan that he is gay. Alan takes no time in taking advantage of this.

characters.name: Paddy O'Rourke
characters.description: Brief Accent Imitation: O'Rourke isn't actually Irish but rather puts it on to help boost ratings in the polls. When explaining this to Alan, he talks with an Irish accent. Shout-Out: The show's fictional counterpart of Labour deputy leader of the time, Roy Hattersley. We know this due to O'Rourke's high standing yet unnamed position in the party, the fact that he is definitely an MP, and the absence of any mention of Hattersley himself. Straight Gay: O'Rourke is revealed to be gay and having affairs with a "lot" of the Labour frontbench. Naturally, B'Stard takes pride in blackmailing him because of it.

characters.name: Sarah B'Stard
characters.description: Depraved Bisexual: As shown in Season 1, she is having an affair with Beatrice while Alan is away. Old Money: Comes from a family that can be traced back to Edward II.

characters.name: Roland Gidleigh-Park
characters.description: Affably Evil: While clearly a heavy bigot, he is much kinder than Alan towards the constituents of Haltemprice.

characters.name: Clarissa Fletcher-Dervish
characters.description: Canon Discontinuity: In Season 1, Piers says that Clarissa, then still unseen, always says that sex is wrong. In the next season, he’s happily sending her letters about being her love slave and her buying toys, implying that this prudishness was retconned. By the time we meet her, she’s very sex positive.

characters.name: Norma Bormann
characters.description: Trans Tribulations: Goes through wanting to change their gender, being miserable as a result of their biological gender.

characters.name: Sidney Bliss
characters.description: Bartender Confidant: Acts as this to Alan. The Storyteller: Likes telling stories about his past. He also seems to take delight in recounting historic execution methods.
